incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: realtime-p99-latency > 1200ms for /v1/generate (global) — paging on-call SRE. Incident ID: INC-2026-1719504322
Alex Chen: Oncall here, picking up. Kicking off quick triage. Anyone seeing obvious deploys?
Priya Rao: I didn't see a deploy in the last 30m. Checking runtime dashboards now — p95 increased modestly but p99 and tail are the issue.
Marta Lopez: Infra autoscaler shows scale events failed to provision 3 nodes around 1719504200. Looks like capacity request latencies spiked in us-west-2.
Alex Chen: Noted. First quick checks: 1) confirm ingestion vs serving (frontend vs runtime) 2) check streaming stall traces 3) check KV cache hit rates.
Priya Rao: Running prometheus queries, posting snippets.
Priya Rao: ```
# p99 over 10m for /v1/generate
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{route="/v1/generate"}[5m])) by (le, zone))
```
Priya Rao: Result: p99 ~ 1.35s in us-west-2, p99 ~ 900ms in eu-west-1. Tail weight concentrated on a few hosts.
Liam Park: Support reports a handful of customers in eu-west experiencing stalled streams and timeouts, one on a dedicated instance (cust-204). They hit retries and saw duplicate generation tokens.
Alex Chen: Can you paste the customer ticket ID? Need to correlate request ids.
Liam Park: Ticket #CS-8792. They've attached a request-id header: req-id=rx-7f4a2c. Seen ~14 failures over 12m.
Priya Rao: Searching logs for that req-id: ```
rg "rx-7f4a2c" /var/log/runtime/streams/*.log | tail -n 40
```
Priya Rao: Found a repeated pattern: streaming connection established, output chunks stop after initial tokens, then connection remains open for ~30s before timeout. Example log lines:
Priya Rao: ```
2026-05-03T12:12:08.123Z [info] req=rx-7f4a2c host=runtime-az2 shard=sh-17 stream_chunk=1
2026-05-03T12:12:08.456Z [warn] req=rx-7f4a2c host=runtime-az2 kvcache=miss model=redwood-xl-2 quantized=false
2026-05-03T12:12:38.789Z [error] req=rx-7f4a2c host=runtime-az2 stall_detected duration=30.3s reason=awaiting-kernel
```
Marta Lopez: That aligns with the node provisioning failures — some hosts reporting high kernel spin/wait. Could be a GPU driver or oomd churn causing stalls for a subset of shards.
Alex Chen: Quick mitigation options: A) move traffic off affected hosts (drain), B) fallback to lower-latency model variant temporarily, C) enable shorter stream chunk timeouts to fail fast and allow client-side retry, D) provision spare burst pool (if infra can). Thoughts?
James O'Neil: From product/customer POV, fallback to lower-cost/latency model variant is acceptable for a short window if we clearly surface degraded quality. We should prioritize customer continuity.
Priya Rao: I can push a routing policy to divert 30% of traffic from runtime-az2 shard group to other healthy shards and simultaneously reduce max batch size for /v1/generate to reduce tail amplification. Command to patch routing policy:
Priya Rao: ```
# quick patch (runtime CLI)
redwood runtime route update --route "/v1/generate" --exclude-hosts runtime-az2 --percentage 30
redwood runtime config set --route "/v1/generate" --max-batch-size 8
```
Alex Chen: Oncall infra, Marta, can you confirm we have capacity in other AZs and that drain won't overload them? Also check GPU driver errors on the flagged hosts: dmesg / syslog for 172.31.25.*
Marta Lopez: Confirmed other AZs have ~15% spare headroom. I'll start drains on two impacted hosts and kick an emergency node health check. Running: ```
ssh infra@172.31.25.18 sudo systemctl status gpu-monitor && sudo journalctl -u runtime-agent -n 200
```
Marta Lopez: gpu-monitor showed repeated HRESULT errors, kernel backtrace at ~1719504180. I'm initiating host drain and marking hosts InService=false in the autoscaler.
Liam Park: I've messaged the affected customers (CS-8792 and a couple more) with a brief note that we're investigating and may route them to a lower-latency model; offering to rollback to non-streaming sync API if they prefer.
Alex Chen: Good. Operational plan: 1) Divert 30% traffic off shard group (Priya) 2) Drain flagged hosts (Marta) 3) Temporarily reduce batch sizes and shorten stream timeouts (Priya) 4) Monitor p95/p99 and errors (Alex) 5) Update customers via support (Liam)
Priya Rao: Patch applied: routing updated and max-batch-size lowered. Also lowered streaming keepalive to 6s to trigger earlier retries for hung streams.
Priya Rao: ```
# verify p99 after patch (5m window)
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{route="/v1/generate"}[5m])) by (le, zone))
# now p99 us-west-2 -> 720ms, eu-west-1 -> 890ms
```
Alex Chen: Nice improvement on p99 in us-west. Keep an eye on error-rate due to early timeouts.
Marta Lopez: Drains completed on the two worst hosts; autoscaler replaced them with new instances, kernel/drivers are clean on replacements. Host-level error counts dropped to baseline.
Liam Park: Customers confirmed improved behavior for CS-8792, they saw successful retries and overall latency better. They asked for postmortem when done.
James O'Neil: Please include customer impact window and mitigation steps in the postmortem. Also note the implication of autoscaler failure path — needs runbook update.
Alex Chen: Agreed. I'll keep the thread live for the next hour for monitoring and start a postmortem doc. Immediate status: majority mitigations applied, p99 back to <800ms for global, streaming stall rate down 84%. We'll transition to incident review and root-cause analysis. If anything regresses, page me.
incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-1719504322 updated: severity=high -> mitigated, assignees=[Alex Chen, Priya Rao, Marta Lopez], incident_channel=#incidents.
Alex Chen: Thanks team. Postmortem owners: Priya (runtime), Marta (infra), James (customer impact). I'll file INC-2026-1719504322/postmortem and link here when created.
Priya Rao: Filing now, will include metric graphs, request traces, exact host ids, and the CLI commands we ran.
Liam Park: Closing customer tickets with a summary.
Alex Chen: Thread resolved for live mitigation. Leaving monitoring on for 45m.
Priya Rao: :white_check_mark:
